findings.title: The FRESH-4 'sound' verdicts behind R1, R3, D3, D11, D13, D14 and 'all four: True' only hold inside each task's own value range. Inputs with negative values flip them
findings.explanation: Sound.verdict draws its fresh inputs (oracles.fresh_inputs) only between the smallest and largest example value and between the shortest and longest example length. Most tasks have no negative example value, so many verified programs that pass rely on xs >= 0. Of the 367 distinct (task, program) pairs stored as sound, 74 disagree with the generating function on wider inputs. The empty list, longer lists and negative values are all in that wider draw, but the failures are almost all negatives: of the 41 failing programs among the discordant tasks, 41 fail on negatives and only 4 on non-negative or longer lists. Typical failures are on [-1], for example (reverse then append-k -2) returns [-2,-2] where [-1,-2] is expected. R3 holds by one task, and 15 of its 54 new-only tasks fail this way against 9 of its 53 generation-0-only tasks. Under the registered in-range definition nothing is wrong. Under the wide reading, R1, R3, D3, D11, D13, D14 and 'all four' fail.

findings.title: Ending 4's 'dreamt' stratum counts dream programs that return lists of booleans as computing list-of-0/1 tasks (True == 1)
findings.explanation: dreamt() at confirm.py:453-462 checks a dream program with `got.value != want or type(got.value) is not type(want)`. The type check is on the top level only, so [True, False] == [1, 0] passes. Three dream programs of type list[int] -> list[bool] (map (gt x1 4) ..., map (is_empty (range (mod x1 k))) ...) are counted as reproducing the 16 examples of identify-* tasks, whose outputs are lists of ints 0/1. Under the DSL's types they do not compute those tasks. The registered wording is 'the FRESH-4 tasks whose 16 examples a dream program of the run reproduces'. All three tasks are solved soundly by new@deploy and by no generation-0 run, so they move new-only tasks out of the undreamt stratum.

findings.title: One correct new@deploy program is stored 'not sound' only because it exceeds the 2,000-step evaluator budget on one in-range input
findings.explanation: Sound._agrees (confirm.py:86-97) treats `not got.ok` as disagreement, with STEPS = 2000. On fresh4::((remove-mod-k 2) (identify-geq-k 7)) the new@deploy program is (map (length (filter (eq x2 5) (range x1)))) after the odd filter. That equals [x >= 7] on odd x. Its step count grows with each value, and on the in-range input [15]*10 it exceeds 2,000 steps. With a larger budget it agrees on all 200 stored-method inputs, and on all 400 of my own in-range draws plus 404 wide ones. It is the only flip under my in-range verdicts. No stored 'sound' verdict flips.

findings.title: R2 'holds with 14 tasks', but in this run its two ablation conditions cannot fail: the ablated rows are record-for-record the cycle-1 row and the generation-0 row
findings.explanation: R2 counts a FRESH-4 task when four things hold: (1) it is a gain after cycle 1, (2) it was built with a recursive symbol, (3) it is lost without the recursive symbols, and (4) it is lost without the first cycle's symbols and everything defined through them (confirm.py lines 593-605, 621-623). In this run all four cycle-2 symbols (s22_1..s25_1) are recursive seeds, and each of them is defined through a cycle-1 symbol. So 'without-recursive' is exactly the cycle-1 vocabulary (15 symbols), and 'without-cycle1-lineage' removes all 19 symbols, which leaves generation 0. Inlining works: spec_without uses each symbol's inlined witness. The two ablated rows are therefore the same runs as cycle1@student:fresh4 and gen0@student:fresh4, and the gain set already excludes both. Conditions (3) and (4) follow from (1) for any program, and with the four seeds, condition (2) only says the program uses a cycle-2 symbol. The code follows the registered text, so this is not a deviation. But the reported chain 14 -> 14 -> 14 -> 14 looks like three independent filters passed, and it is not. R2 here amounts to: 14 FRESH-4 tasks that the cycle-2 vocabulary solves soundly at 10^4 and that generation 0 and the cycle-1 vocabulary do not, each built with a cycle-2 symbol. The same step also loses 9 tasks, so the net is +5.
findings.observed: cycle1@student:fresh4 vs new-without-recursive@student:fresh4: record diffs 0, program diffs 0, sound equal True. gen0@student:fresh4 vs new-without-cycle1-lineage@student:fresh4: record diffs 0, program diffs 0, sound equal True. The lineage ablation removes all 19 symbols. The recursive set and the cycle-2 symbols are the same set: ['s22_1','s23_1','s24_1','s25_1']. Each seed's folded program matches a cycle-2 discovery text for text (s22_1 far2/remove-index-k k=3; s23_1 seven append-k/append-index-k tasks; s24_1 near/pow-k k=5; s25_1 far/count-head-in-tail).
findings.evidence: I checked confirm.json myself. cycle1@student:fresh4 and new-without-recursive@student:fresh4 differ in 0 records, and their programs and sound sets are equal. gen0@student:fresh4 and new-without-cycle1-lineage@student:fresh4 also differ in 0 records, with equal programs and sound sets. recursion.recursive_symbols equals with_the_symbols_defined_through_them, and both are ['s22_1','s23_1','s24_1','s25_1'], which are the cycle-2 symbols. The without-recursive ablation removes exactly those four. The without-cycle1-lineage ablation removes all 19 symbols. In confirm.py's second(), gains4 = new minus cycle1 minus gen0, so 'lost without recursive' (subtracting the cycle1 row) and 'lost without lineage' (subtracting the gen0 row) take nothing out of the gains. The chain in the tables reads 14->14->14->14 (addendum8_tables.txt line 151). Ablation detail: 14 tasks lost and 9 gained without the recursive symbols.
findings.effect_on_results: R2 = True and D12 = PASS do not change. Only the wording changes. R2 on FRESH-4 comes down to 14 tasks that the cycle-2 vocabulary solves soundly at 10^4, that neither generation 0 nor cycle 1 solves, and whose programs use a cycle-2 symbol. The two ablation filters add no evidence in this run, and the cycle-2 step is a net +5 (14 gained, 9 lost).

findings.title: The lead lives on stage instances that the development set FRESH-3 showed the new vocabulary solving; where it did not, the lead is 7 against 6
findings.explanation: 68 of the 75 new-only FRESH-4 tasks have both stage instances in FRESH-3 tasks that new@deploy solves soundly (55 with both in the same position). Only 14 of the 20 control-only tasks do (9 in the same position). On the 302 list tasks with both instances seen solved on FRESH-3 it is 153 against 99 (68 against 14). On the other 454 it is 18 against 17 (7 against 6). The variant was chosen after reading FRESH-3, so the lead is concentrated on what development had seen working. This overlaps largely with the first finding, since those instances are the symbol stages. The lead per task shrinks from 13.6 to 7.3 per 100 list tasks (FRESH-3: 84 against 55 of 213, recomputed; FRESH-4: 171 against 116 of 756). The discordant ratio falls from 36:7 to 75:20.
